description: Hassium is a synthetic chemical element with symbol Hs and atomic number 108 that is highly radioactive, with its most stable known isotopes having half-lives of about ten seconds. It is a superheavy transactinide element and a member of period 7 and group 8, making it the sixth member of the 6d series of transition metals. Natural occurrences of hassium have been hypothesized but never found.
uses: Chemistry experiments have confirmed that hassium behaves as the heavier homologue to osmium, reacting readily with oxygen to form a volatile tetroxide.
characteristics: Hassium is highly radioactive with most stable known isotopes having half-lives of about ten seconds. One of its isotopes, 270Hs, has magic numbers of protons and neutrons for deformed nuclei, giving it greater stability against spontaneous fission. The chemical properties of hassium compare well with the chemistry of other group 8 elements.
